neighbours.label: The tokens ' comments' / ' comment' / ' commentary' (reader-comment invitations, 'see comments', 'a commentary on'); weaker, scattered firing on 'below'/'here' pointers and misc tokens
fire: Thanks for stopping by the shop today, and we always welcome your comments about the new layout before the weekend sale.
If you disagree with the ranking, say so in the comments and I will gladly revise the list next month.
The editor added a short commentary on the court ruling, which ran alongside the full transcript of the hearing.
For the Latin text and its variants, see the comments to verse twelve in the older scholarly edition.
We read every message sent to the club, so leave your comments after the recipe and tell us how the bread turned out.
The film critic closed her column with a witty commentary on how modern sequels recycle their own plots.
Please share your thoughts in the comments section if you have ever hiked this trail in winter.
Readers who wish to comment on the proposed zoning change may do so until the end of the month, and every comment will be logged.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, random arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top examples are mostly ' comments'/' comment'/' commentary' but the pole is broad (6.6% of tokens above 0.1 of max) and band samples above 0.3 are a scattered mix (',', digits, '.gov', 'to'), so the word label likely covers only a small part of the pole. Fire items use the comment words; near misses use feedback/remarks/notes synonyms in matching frames.
